business_problem: SEP2 needed to eliminate the alert-analysis bottleneck in its security operations center, where analysts were spending up to 20 minutes gathering context for a single event and risking backlogs during threat spikes.
solution_summary: SEP2 built an ecosystem of custom security agents on Gemini platform and Google Security Operations to automate the repetitive parts of threat triage while keeping human analysts focused on higher-value investigations. The company defines specialized agent personas such as triage agents and threat-intelligence agents that pull data from firewalls, endpoints, and external feeds, then use Gemini reasoning to summarize findings and support faster remediation. These workflows also help engineers create new threat-detection rules far faster by turning natural-language inputs into programmatic logic. SEP2 designed the environment with customer-data isolation and UK residency requirements in mind, using Google Cloud controls so client data is kept separate and never used to train public models. The roadmap extends toward continuous threat-hunting agents and a self-healing SOC where verified threats can trigger automated containment in seconds.

data_flow: When a new alert fires, SEP2's triage and threat-intelligence agents gather evidence from firewalls, endpoints, and external feeds, reason over the combined context with Gemini, and present a standardized summary to human analysts who can approve remediation or continue deeper investigation.
business_outcome: SEP2 now writes threat-detection rules six times faster, triages new security alerts 20 times faster, avoids analyst burnout during high-volume periods, and is building toward proactive continuous threat hunting and automated containment.
